# `brief.set`: Set brief

Records what the user asked for (category, style, size, budget, must-haves) as checks the model is measured against.

- Category: spec
- Version: 1
- Complexity: O(size of the brief)
- Flags: undoable
- Also known as: brief, requirements, intent, goals, acceptance

A brief expands into checks: its size (one value means within 10%) and triangle budget, its category's defaults (a humanoid head is symmetric and closed, anchored parts touch what they sit on, proportions within the style's range), each `must_have` feature (parts named after it or tagged with it) with measurable traits (`length_ratio_to_<part>`), and each `must_not` (`<a>_penetrating_<b>`). A spec answers the brief by naming it; every report then carries the coverage line. Items that need later phases are listed as pending.

**Use for** turning the user's words into tests before modelling.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brief` | `unknown` | required | The brief: title, category, style, size, budget, must_have, must_not, references (see the spec guide). |
| `name` | `string` | required | Name of the brief; a spec answers it with `"brief": "<name>"`. |

## Examples

```json
{"brief":{"budget":{"tris":[8000,14000]},"category":"humanoid_head","must_have":[{"count":2,"feature":"ear","traits":{"length_ratio_to_head":[0.35,0.6],"pointiness":"high"}}],"size":{"height":"0.26m"},"style":"stylized","title":"Elf ranger head"},"name":"elf"}
```

Result: `brief elf: 10 checks: height 234 to 286 mm; budget 8,000 to 14,000 tris; symmetric across x; head closed; parts attached to what they sit on; width_to_height 0.62 to 1; depth_to_height 0.7 to 1.15; eye_line 0.35 to 0.62; 2 ear; ear length 0.35 to 0.6 of head (1 pending)`
